granular.exposure_details_notes:
**For the last 5 years plus the estimate for the year quoted, we need the best guess exposure data including acquisitions** unless acquisitions have limited prior acts cover, in which case we need those acquisitions exposure data back to their retro date or for the last 5 years, whichever is the more recent) **but excluding divestments and excluded entities**. The last 5 years data will affect both exposure and experience (burning cost) rating.

**The exposure data prior to 5 years ago should be the sum of that year's exposure data for all covered entities whose claims data you have.** You don't need to provide exposure data for years earlier than 5 years prior to the Policy Year noted in cell D6 of the Claims sheet.
If for a certain entity(ies) you have data back to a more recent year than the Policy Year noted in cell D6 of the Claims sheet, you will need to include that entity(ies) exposure data for the years where you have their claims data AND for 5 years prior to that. These years data will only affect experience (burning cost) rating, so if only require to match claims data for these years other than anything else.

•  Only input country and state-splits in the Policy Years available.

rate_change.instructions:
The rate change tab calculates the change in premium associated with each component (detailed descriptions in the table below). The most appropriate method to obtain a rate change is to calculate the change on premium rather than the change in underlying factors as there are numerous interactions and products to consider.

                    To calculate the rate change, please follow the steps below:
                    1) The user should fist click 'Fetch Expiring Data' to initialise the rate change calculation.
                    2) Select mapping between renewing layers and expiry, this needs to be a 1-1 mapping. For new layers that do not have any link to expiring layer, set the expiring layer to the blank value.
                    3) If there have been any changes to the previous tabs (including the first instance of reaching this tab in any record/YOA), please press 'Calculate Rate Change'.
                    4) The rater will derive the rate changes to each component from the user input.
                    5) The user will be able to override the rate change values as appropriate in the 'UW Selected %' column.
                    6) To recalculate rate change following further changes, please press 'Calculate Rate Change' again.
                    7) Following the task running, the user will be able to override 'Expiring' and 'Renewal' fields with rate change automatically calculating WITHOUT having to run the task again. 

                    _Rate Change Components Include:_
                    _**Exposure Change**_: Driven by changes to base premium due to market cap, assets, country, industry, and ADR percentage
                    _**Risk Characteristics Change**_: Driven by changes to schedule modifiers
                    _**Deductible Change**_: Driven by changes to excesses, and deductibles
                    _**Limit Change**_: Driven by changes to limits 
                    _**Terms and Conditions Change**_: Driven by changes to coverages selected
                    _**Other Change**_: Driven by any other factors such as brokerage

hover_info.blended_model_net_rate: Includes CAT load and NMP load.
hover_info.blended_uw_net_rate:
Includes:
 - Wordings Adjustment
 - UW Adjustment
 - CAT load and NMP load
hover_info.calculated_policy_year: The earliest 5 years notional revenue is back calculated, based on the annual growth rate.
hover_info.elevated_risk_year_load:
May include:
 - Increased economic risk
 - Recession
 - Higher than normal claims inflation.
hover_info.expected_loss_cost_net:
- Net of non loss cost provisions
 - Net of brokerage
hover_info.gross_rate_per_mill: This is the gross rate based on the Bound Premium. It includes the non loss cost provisions.
hover_info.ilf_gross_benchmark_premium:
ILF Implied Experience Rate is shown for imformation only.

This approach provides a hybrid experience-exposure rate, whereby:
1) Emprical losses are used to price up to the attritional cap (experience rating)
2) The ILFs then used to extrapolate to the full policy limit (exposure rating)
hover_info.inception_date: Inception Date used to calulate the IBNR.
hover_info.latest_policy_year: Best guess for upcoming policy year, NOT the last completed policy year.
hover_info.retention_residual: Residual retention after Agg is fully eroded.
hover_info.retention_underlying: Underlying to EEC and Agg is fully eroded.
hover_info.rtc: For RTC deals, please keep Limit Agg and Excess Agg empty.
hover_info.territory_policy_year: Please leave blank unless you happend to have splits for the upcoming policy year.
hover_info.total_usd_inflated: The claims post retention structure is fed into the experience rating.
hover_info.uw_experience_weighting:
- If Experience Rate is higher, then full credibility is given.
 - If Experience Rate is lower, then only 20% credibility is given.
hover_info.value_of_claims_data: Accounts for exposure revaluing, exposure weighting and general IBNR.

experience_rating.claims_instructions: **Claims data needs to align with exposure data.** Unless there is less than 5 years of prior retro cover for some/all entities (see Exposure Details tab for more info), that means **we need claims data for all entities, including acquisitions but excluding divestments and excluded entities, going back 5 policy years,**then **prior to that** you include **claims and exposuure data for entities only where you have claims information for that entity for that year** (clean or otherwise).
experience_rating.experience_instructions:
**Limitations**
1) Experience rating does not allow for the Round The Clock (RTC) arrangements.For insureds with RTC towers, these insureds will be priced as aggregate placements.

2) Experience Rating will price all layers as Defence Costs inclusive, regardless of which option is selected for ‘Defence Costs in Addition’ in the Structure & Pricing tab. (N.B. Experience Rating will, however, take account of whether you select Yes or No to ‘Also applies to defence cost?’ for the retention)

3) ILF implied Gross Benchmark Premium is used for information only for the high XS layers which lack claims in the past.The limitation is that ILF only allows AOC limit, which does not allow aggregate.

granular.exposure_details_notes:
**For the last 5 years plus the estimate for the year quoted, we need the best guess exposure data including acquisitions** unless acquisitions have limited prior acts cover, in which case we need those acquisitions exposure data back to their retro date or for the last 5 years, whichever is the more recent) **but excluding divestments and excluded entities**. The last 5 years data will affect both exposure and experience (burning cost) rating.

**The exposure data prior to 5 years ago should be the sum of that year's exposure data for all covered entities whose claims data you have.** You don't need to provide exposure data for years earlier than 5 years prior to the Policy Year.
If for a certain entity(ies) you have data back to a more recent year than the Policy Year, you will need to include that entity(ies) exposure data for the years where you have their claims data AND for 5 years prior to that. These years data will only affect experience (burning cost) rating, so if only require to match claims data for these years other than anything else.

The CAT load for Lawyers has been estimated based on the subprime mortgage crisis.

This load is in addition to the CAT load which is already baked into the model's rates and which was based upon the subprime mortgage crisis.

 - Higher than normal claims inflation.

- Net of non loss cost provisions

hover_info.gross_benchmark_premium:
Include 70% LR and Brokerage.

Note: This will not fully align with the implied 100% experience gros benchmark premium on the S&P tab, as the CAT load applies to the latter.
hover_info.gross_rate_per_mill: This is the gross rate based on the Bound Premium. It includes the non loss cost provisions.
hover_info.ilf_gross_benchmark_premium:
ILF Implied Experience Rate is shown for imformation only.

This approach provides a hybrid experience-exposure rate, whereby:
1) Emprical losses are used to price up to the attritional cap (experience rating)
2) The ILFs then used to extrapolate to the full policy limit (exposure rating)

rate_change.instructions:
The rate change tab calculates the change in premium associated with each component (detailed descriptions in the table below). The most appropriate method to obtain a rate change is to calculate the change on premium rather than the change in underlying factors as there are numerous interactions and products to consider.

                    To calculate the rate change, please follow the steps below:
                    1) The user should fist click 'Fetch Expiring Data' to initialise the rate change calculation.
                    2) Select mapping between renewing layers and expiry, this needs to be a 1-1 mapping. For new layers that do not have any link to expiring layer, set the expiring layer to the blank value.
                    3) If there have been any changes to the previous tabs (including the first instance of reaching this tab in any record/YOA), please press 'Calculate Rate Change'.
                    4) The rater will derive the rate changes to each component from the user input.
                    5) The user will be able to override the rate change values as appropriate in the 'UW Selected %' column.
                    6) To recalculate rate change following further changes, please press 'Calculate Rate Change' again.
                    7) Following the task running, the user will be able to override 'Expiring' and 'Renewal' fields with rate change automatically calculating WITHOUT having to run the task again. 

                    _Rate Change Components Include:_
                    _**Exposure Change**_: Driven by changes to base premium due to market cap, assets, country, industry, and ADR percentage
                    _**Risk Characteristics Change**_: Driven by changes to schedule modifiers
                    _**Deductible Change**_: Driven by changes to excesses, and deductibles
                    _**Limit Change**_: Driven by changes to limits 
                    _**Terms and Conditions Change**_: Driven by changes to coverages selected
                    _**Other Change**_: Driven by any other factors such as brokerage
